brief: Design an interface for a "Temporal Recipe Reconstructor" that helps users reverse-engineer forgotten family recipes by mapping flavor memories to ingredients through an interactive taste wheel that m

dominant_strengths: Warm cream/tan palette with amber category labels evokes nostalgia and food memory, fitting the temporal/recipe theme well
Clean serif-ish header paired with restrained sans body creates a calm, archival tone appropriate for memory work
Pill tokens are legibly typeset and consistently rounded, giving the chip system a tactile, edible-feeling craft
dominant_weaknesses: Brief promises an 'interactive taste wheel' but the design is a flat two-column drag-bin — the central spatial metaphor is missing
Empty drop zone dominates 60% of canvas with no scaffolding, preview, or reconstruction logic visible — looks unfinished
Left panel is cropped at 'First taste' and pills wrap inconsistently (two columns then one), revealing weak grid discipline
fix_priorities: Replace the rectangular drop zone with the radial taste wheel implied by the brief, with axes for time/intensity/memory
Show a populated example state: ingredient suggestions, confidence rings, or a reconstructed recipe forming as tokens land
Fix the chip grid (uniform 2-col or flowing rows) and ensure no category gets clipped at viewport edge
Introduce micro-interactions — drag shadows, magnetic snapping, ingredient inference — to express the 'reconstruct' verb
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral warmth carries the piece, but behavioral affordances are thin and the reflective payoff (seeing a recipe emerge) is entirely absent.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially solves the brief — the memory-token vocabulary is on-theme, but the promised taste wheel and reverse-engineering output are not shown.
